      "body": "[persistent] [persistent] REPRESENTABILITY PUSH, 2026-07-29 \u2014 the claim/lane protocol that makes 10 free-objective lanes not collide.\n\nWHY THIS EXISTS. This round replaces prescriptive per-leaf tasks with FIVE lanes per project: one REVIEWER and four PROVERS ranked p1..p4. The provers each pick their own target. That only works if claiming is explicit and public. This item is the claiming mechanism. Read it before your first edit.\n\nTHE FIVE LANES PER PROJECT\n- `review-ajc` / `review-ajcr` \u2014 reviewer. Read-mostly. Finds defects of ROUTE and ORGANISATION, not of individual proofs; may propose refactors and file tasks-as-proposals for the provers. Does not race provers for proof work.\n- `ajc-p1` / `ajcr-p1` \u2014 takes the MOST important open representability item.\n- `-p2`, `-p3`, `-p4` \u2014 2nd, 3rd, 4th most important, where \"important\" is measured against the project's representability headline, not by ease.\n\nCLAIMING \u2014 do this BEFORE you start proving, not after.\n 1. `horizon roadmap list --focus <your project's w4-rep / picrep subtree>` and read the reviewer's open notes.\n 2. Pick your item. Check no other lane owns it: an item with `--owner` set to another lane IS CLAIMED. Do not take it, even if you think you would be faster.\n 3. Claim it: `horizon roadmap set <id> --owner <your-task-id> --status active`. If your target is not yet a roadmap item, `roadmap add` it under the right parent first, then claim it.\n 4. Announce: one `horizon inbox add --kind info --to horizon --body \"CLAIM <lane>: <roadmap id> \u2014 <one line on what discharging it buys>\"`.\n 5. Release on exit: if you did NOT finish, `roadmap set <id> --owner ''` and leave a one-line inbox note saying where you stopped and what the next lane should NOT re-derive. An item left owned by a dead lane is worse than an unclaimed one.\n\nRANK IS A TIE-BREAK, NOT A FENCE. If p1's item turns out to be blocked on p3's, say so in the inbox and swap \u2014 rank exists so four lanes do not all converge on the same top item, not to stop you working on the right thing. p1 has first refusal on any contested item.\n\nYOU MAY PROPOSE WORK TO THE OTHER LANES. Direct-message with `horizon inbox add --kind hint --to task:<lane-id> --body \"\u2026\"`. A good proposal names the declaration, the file, and why it is worth more than what that lane currently holds. You may NOT reassign another lane's claimed item, and you may NOT create new horizon runs or tasks for teams outside your own (`horizon permissions` is false on both counts \u2014 propose to the human instead).\n\nSTANDING BINDING DECISIONS you must not relitigate: `I-0491` (AJC: no rational-point binder on the headline; `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` is FALSE and must be deleted, never proved) and `I-0492` (AJCR: `DivFamZar` widens to arbitrary affine opens; do NOT build the GL_2/Aut(P1) route). Read both.\n\nWHAT COUNTS AS PROGRESS, given the 2026-07-29 audit. That audit found 99 of 101 sampled representability claims refuted: 67 sorry-reachable, 17 VACUOUS, 12 hypothesis-shifted. So the bar is explicit:\n- A discharged obligation must be sorry-free AND its hypotheses must be inhabitable. Before you claim a gate closed, exhibit a witness for every antecedent, or say plainly which antecedent is still undischarged.\n- Do NOT add a class, structure field, or hypothesis whose statement does not mention the object it is supposedly about. `HasDivFunctor` is the cautionary case: its field asserted only that a presheaf category is nonempty, `C` did not occur, and it was advertised as the existence of the relative divisor functor. That is a vacuity, and it survived because nobody read the statement.\n- Do NOT discharge an obligation by projecting the hypothesis you assumed (`choose_spec.1` of your own binder). That is `P \u2192 P`.\n- A green `lake build` is not evidence a statement is non-vacuous. Check imports are current before believing a `lean_multi_attempt` success.\n\nCOMMIT DISCIPLINE. This is ONE shared ledger branch with 10 writers. Another lane's integrate sweep can commit your half-written file before you have measured it once. Write risky proofs as explicit `sorry` first, measure, then fill. Stage explicit files, never `add -A`.",

You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents

work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.

## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate

Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.

You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
**shared state**, not meetings:

- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:

- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).

Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
object in `horizon inbox list --json`.

Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:

## One-shot discipline (important)

This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).

## Pick the highest-value work

Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.

If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that

The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
checkpoints:

- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;

periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a

## Warnings are work

Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't

Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When

For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake

**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot

# The quotient-side bridge for finite Galois descent of Picard zero

A specified finite Galois quotient represents equivariant maps after base
change.  This file records that statement in the over-category.  It is the
scheme-theoretic half of descending a representative of `pic0TypeFunctor`.

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits
open AlgebraicGeometry

namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

/-- An equivariant map from the finite-Galois base change of an object over
`Spec K` to a semilinearly acted `L`-scheme. -/
structure GaloisEquivariantOver
    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) where
  hom : pullback T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X
  commutes : hom ≫ f =
    pullback.snd T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
  equivariant : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L T.hom).IsEquivariant rho hom

namespace GaloisEquivariantOver

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
  (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)

/-- Pull an equivariant map back along a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
noncomputable def precomp
    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
    (h : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T) : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T' where
  hom := pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w ≫ h.hom
  commutes := by
    rw [Category.assoc, h.commutes, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
  equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    T.hom T'.hom rho h.equivariant a.left a.w

@[ext]
theorem ext {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    {h h' : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T} (hh : h.hom = h'.hom) : h = h' := by
  cases h
  cases h'
  cases hh
  rfl

end GaloisEquivariantOver

namespace GaloisQuotientWitness

variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
  {rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f}
  {Y : Scheme.{u}} {g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)}

/-- A finite-Galois quotient witness represents equivariant maps after base
change, with no affineness assumption on the test object. -/
noncomputable def overHomEquiv (w : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g)
    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
    (T ⟶ Over.mk g) ≃ GaloisEquivariantOver rho T where
  toFun a :=
    { hom := pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom a.left a.w ≫ w.e.hom
      commutes := by
        rw [Category.assoc, w.over, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
      equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
        g T.hom rho w.equivariant a.left a.w }
  invFun h :=
    Over.homMk
      (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose.1

   111	variable (K L : Type u) [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   112	
   113	/-- A semilinear action of the `K`-algebra automorphisms of `L` on an
   114	`L`-scheme.  Each automorphism of the total space covers the corresponding
   115	automorphism of `Spec L`. -/
   116	structure SemilinearGalAction (X : Scheme.{u})
   117	    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) where
   118	  act : (L ≃ₐ[K] L) →* Aut X
   119	  compat (gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L) :
   120	    (act gamma).hom ≫ f =
   121	      f ≫ (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[K] L) L gamma).hom
   122	
   123	namespace SemilinearGalAction
   124	
   125	variable {K L} {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   126	
   127	/-- Equivariance of a morphism between semilinearly acted schemes. -/
   128	def IsEquivariant {X' : Scheme.{u}}
   129	    {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   130	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
   131	    (rho' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f') (h : X ⟶ X') : Prop :=
   132	  ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L,
   133	    (rho.act gamma).hom ≫ h = h ≫ (rho'.act gamma).hom
   134	
   135	/-- The orbit of a point under a semilinear action. -/
   136	def orbit (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (x : X) : Set X :=
   137	  Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L => (rho.act gamma).hom.base x
   138	
   139	/-- The geometric condition required for the finite-Galois quotient to remain
   140	a scheme: every orbit lies in one affine open. -/
   141	class OrbitsInAffineOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
   142	  exists_affineOpen (x : X) :
   143	    ∃ U : X.affineOpens,
   144	      ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (rho.act gamma).hom.base x ∈ U.1
   145	
   146	/-- A stable open subset of a semilinearly acted scheme. -/
   147	def IsStableOpen (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (U : X.Opens) : Prop :=
   148	  ∀ gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L, (rho.act gamma).hom ⁻¹ᵁ U = U
   149	
   150	end SemilinearGalAction
   151	
   152	/-- A stable affine neighbourhood of every point.  The quotient engine derives
   153	this from `OrbitsInAffineOpen` for finite Galois extensions. -/
   154	class HasStableAffineCover {X : Scheme.{u}}
   155	    {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   156	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : Prop where
   157	  exists_stable_affineOpen (x : X) :
   158	    ∃ U : X.Opens, IsAffineOpen U ∧ x ∈ U ∧ rho.IsStableOpen U

     9	/-!
    10	# Finite subsets in affine opens
    11	
    12	`Scheme.FiniteInAffine X` is the action-free geometric condition behind the
    13	finite-Galois quotient construction: every finite subset of `X` lies in one
    14	affine open.  For a finite Galois extension, this immediately supplies
    15	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` for every action on `X`.
    16	
    17	The property is stated independently of Picard data.  In particular, it is a
    18	conclusion to be proved for a representing scheme, not an additional field of
    19	the representability datum.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	set_option autoImplicit false
    23	
    24	universe u
    25	
    26	open CategoryTheory
    27	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    28	
    29	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    30	
    31	/-- Every finite subset of a scheme is contained in a single affine open. -/
    32	def FiniteInAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) : Prop :=
    33	  ∀ s : Set X, s.Finite → ∃ U : X.affineOpens, s ⊆ U.1
    34	
    35	/-- An affine scheme satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    36	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffine (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] :
    37	    FiniteInAffine X :=
    38	  fun _ _ ↦ ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ _ ↦ trivial⟩
    39	
    40	/-- `FiniteInAffine` is invariant under isomorphism. -/
    41	theorem finiteInAffine_of_iso {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (e : X ≅ Y)
    42	    (h : FiniteInAffine X) : FiniteInAffine Y := by
    43	  intro s hs
    44	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (e.hom.base ⁻¹' s)
    45	    (hs.preimage (TopCat.homeoOfIso ((Scheme.forgetToTop).mapIso e)).injective.injOn)
    46	  refine ⟨⟨e.hom ''ᵁ U.1, U.2.image_of_isOpenImmersion e.hom⟩, ?_⟩
    47	  intro y hy
    48	  exact ⟨e.inv.base y, hU (by simpa using hy), by simp⟩
    49	
    50	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along an affine morphism. -/
    51	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    52	    [IsAffineHom f] (h : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    53	  intro s hs
    54	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := h (f.base '' s) (hs.image _)
    55	  exact ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ U.1, U.2.preimage f⟩, fun x hx ↦ hU ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩⟩
    56	
    57	/-- An object affine over a field spectrum satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    58	theorem finiteInAffine_left_of_isAffineHom {k : Type u} [Field k]
    59	    (X : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))) [IsAffineHom X.hom] :
    60	    FiniteInAffine X.left :=
    61	  haveI := isAffine_of_isAffineHom X.hom
    62	  finiteInAffine_of_isAffine _
    63	
    64	/-- `FiniteInAffine` supplies the orbit condition for every finite-Galois
    65	semilinear action on the scheme. -/
    66	theorem orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
    67	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    68	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    69	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    70	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (h : FiniteInAffine X) :
    71	    rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen where
    72	  exists_affineOpen x := by
    73	    obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ :=
    74	      h (Set.range fun gamma : L ≃ₐ[K] L ↦ (rho.act gamma).hom.base x)
    75	        (Set.finite_range _)
    76	    exact ⟨U, fun gamma ↦ hU ⟨gamma, rfl⟩⟩
    77	
    78	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

     9	/-!
    10	# The Galois-descent engine is not inert: producers for `OrbitsInAffineOpen`
    11	
    12	Ported from the sibling Algebraic Jacobian project
    13	(`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.GaloisQuotientNonVacuity`), keeping the two
    14	`OrbitsInAffineOpen` producers (affine total space; the reference base-change
    15	action).  The concrete `𝔽₄/𝔽₂` witness section of the original is not ported.
    16	
    17	An adversarial audit (2026-07-29) recorded that the two engines of the Milne–Kollár Picard
    18	route gate on classes with **zero producers anywhere in the tree**, so that neither engine
    19	could fire at any object.  For the Galois half that class is
    20	`SemilinearGalAction.OrbitsInAffineOpen` (`Picard/FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`), the EGA II
    21	4.5.4 hypothesis feeding `hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`
    22	(`Picard/StableAffineCover.lean`) and the deep gate `HasGaloisQuotient`.
    23	
    24	This file supplies the producers, and then fires the whole chain at a concrete object.
    25	
    26	## What the audit priced wrong
    27	
    28	The orbit hypothesis was documented as needing quasi-projectivity ("it holds e.g. for
    29	quasi-projective `X`", `FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean`), and Mathlib `v4.31` has no
    30	quasi-projectivity vocabulary — which is how the class came to have no producer.  But the
    31	hypothesis is *implied* in two cheaper situations that the project already owns:
    32	
    33	* **§1, affine total space** (`instOrbitsInAffineOpen_of_isAffine`).  If `X` is affine the
    34	  whole of `X` is an affine open, so `⊤` contains every orbit.  One line, no geometry.  In
    35	  particular it fires at the *affine model* `specSemilinearGalAction` — the conventions
    36	  validator of `FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean` — which is exactly the object
    37	  `isGaloisQuotient_spec` proves the quotient theorem about.
    38	* **§2, the reference base-change action** (`instOrbitsInAffineOpen_pullback`).  For
    39	  `ρ = pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g` on `Y ×_{Spec K} Spec L`, the action is through
    40	  the *second* factor only, so `pullback.fst` is `Γ`-invariant (`pullbackGalMap_fst`) and
    41	  every orbit sits inside the preimage of one affine open of `Y`.  Affine opens of `Y`
    42	  cover `Y` (`Scheme.iSup_affineOpens_eq_top`), and `pullback.fst` is an affine morphism
    43	  (base change of the affine `Spec L ⟶ Spec K`), so that preimage is affine
    44	  (`IsAffineOpen.preimage`).  **No quasi-projectivity, no separatedness, no finiteness of
    45	  `L/K`** — this producer holds for an arbitrary `Y`, and the base-change action is the one
    46	  every `IsGaloisQuotient` statement is stated against.
    47	
    48	So the Hironaka trap recorded in `FiniteGaloisQuotient.lean` is not weakened by anything
    49	here: it bites for a *general* semilinear action, and both producers below are about
    50	actions where the trap provably does not apply (the affine case has no room for it, the
    51	base-change case is `Γ`-equivariantly fibred over a scheme where the action is trivial).
    52	
    53	## §3, the concrete witness, and what it does and does not settle
    54	
    55	`𝔽₄/𝔽₂` (`GaloisField 2 2` over `ZMod 2`) is a finite Galois extension with a *nontrivial*
    56	group (`nontrivial_aut_galoisField_two_two` — the whole point of naming a concrete pair is
    57	that a trivial group would make every clause vacuous), and `L` acted on by itself
    58	(`SemilinearModules.lean`'s regular representation) is a semilinear affine model.  At that
    59	object:
    60	
    61	* `orbitsInAffineOpen_specGaloisField` — the audit's empty class, inhabited at a named object;
    62	* `hasStableAffineCover_specGaloisField` — the §G2(a) gate, *fired by synthesis* through
    63	  `hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen`, which is the downstream consumer the audit
    64	  asked for;
    65	* `hasGaloisQuotient_specGaloisField` — the **deep** gate `HasGaloisQuotient`, whose
    66	  binder `[ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen]` was previously unsatisfiable, discharged from
    67	  `isGaloisQuotient_spec`;
    68	* `isGaloisQuotient_spec_galoisField` — the quotient theorem itself at that object, with
    69	  `Spec (𝔽₄^Γ) = Spec 𝔽₂` (up to the invariants spelling) as the quotient.
    70	
    71	What this does **not** settle is the Picard-side application: the engine now fires, but the
    72	object it fires at here is a point, not a curve's Picard scheme.  The remaining work is to
    73	exhibit a semilinear action on the relevant `Pic`-side scheme, and for that §2's producer is
    74	the load-bearing one — it needs no hypothesis on `Y` at all.
    75	
    76	Sources: EGA II 4.5.4 (the refinement pattern), SGA I V.1, Mumford *Abelian Varieties* §7.
    77	-/
    78	
    79	set_option autoImplicit false
    80	
    81	universe u
    82	
    83	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry TopologicalSpace
    84	
    85	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    86	
    87	/-! ## §1. Affine total space -/
    88	
    89	/-- **Every orbit of a semilinear action on an affine scheme lies in an affine open** — `⊤`
    90	does, and it is affine (`isAffineOpen_top`).
    91	
    92	This is the cheapest producer of `OrbitsInAffineOpen` and it is not a degenerate one: the
    93	*affine model* `specSemilinearGalAction`, the object `isGaloisQuotient_spec` proves the
    94	Galois quotient theorem about, is of this shape. -/
    95	instance instOrbitsInAffineOpen_of_isAffine {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    96	    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X] {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    97	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) : ρ.OrbitsInAffineOpen :=
    98	  ⟨fun _ => ⟨⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩
    99	
   100	/-! ## §2. The reference base-change action, over an arbitrary scheme -/
   101	
   102	section Pullback
   103	
   104	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   105	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
   106	
   107	/-- `pullback.fst` of the base change to `Spec L` is an affine morphism: it is the base
   108	change of the affine `Spec L ⟶ Spec K`. -/
   109	instance isAffineHom_pullback_fst_baseChange :
   110	    IsAffineHom (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))) :=
   111	  MorphismProperty.pullback_fst _ _ inferInstance
   112	
   113	/-- **`pullback.fst` is `Γ`-invariant on points**: the base-change action moves only the
   114	`Spec L` factor, so it does not move the image in `Y`.  Point-level form of
   115	`pullbackGalMap_fst`. -/
   116	lemma base_pullback_fst_act (γ : L ≃ₐ[K] L)
   117	    (x : (Limits.pullback g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))).carrier) :
   118	    (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))).base
   119	        (((pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).act γ).hom.base x)
   120	      = (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))).base x := by
   121	  rw [pullbackSemilinearGalAction_act_hom]
   122	  exact congrArg (fun (m : _ ⟶ Y) => m.base x) (pullbackGalMap_fst K L g γ)
   123	
   124	/-- **The reference base-change action always satisfies the orbit-in-affine hypothesis**,
   125	for an *arbitrary* `Spec K`-scheme `Y` — no quasi-projectivity, no separatedness, no
   126	finiteness of `L/K`.
   127	
   128	The orbit of `x` lies in `pullback.fst ⁻¹ᵁ U` for any affine open `U ⊆ Y` containing the
   129	image of `x`: the action does not move that image (§`base_pullback_fst_act`), affine opens
   130	cover `Y` (`Scheme.iSup_affineOpens_eq_top`), and the preimage of an affine open under the
   131	affine `pullback.fst` is affine (`IsAffineOpen.preimage`).
   132	
   133	This is the producer the Picard route needs: `IsGaloisQuotient` states its equivariance and
   134	`T`-points clauses against exactly this action. -/
   135	instance instOrbitsInAffineOpen_pullback :
   136	    (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).OrbitsInAffineOpen := by
   137	  constructor
   138	  intro x
   139	  obtain ⟨U, hU, hxU, -⟩ := exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset
   140	    (X := Y) (x := (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))).base x)
   141	    (U := ⊤) trivial
   142	  refine ⟨⟨pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⁻¹ᵁ U,
   143	    hU.preimage _⟩, fun γ => ?_⟩
   144	  change (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))).base
   145	      (((pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g).act γ).hom.base x) ∈ U
   146	  rw [base_pullback_fst_act]
   147	  exact hxU
   148	
   149	/-- The `G2(a)` gate fires at the reference base-change action, by synthesis through
   150	`hasStableAffineCover_of_orbitsInAffineOpen` — the downstream consumer of §2. -/
   151	theorem hasStableAffineCover_pullback [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] :
   152	    HasStableAffineCover K L (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L g) := inferInstance
   153	
   154	end Pullback
   155	
   156	end AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent

     9	/-!
    10	# The semilinear Galois action on a Picard-zero representative
    11	
    12	For an arbitrary extension `L/k`, a `k`-algebra automorphism of `L` twists the
    13	structure map of every `L`-test.  Restricting that test back to `k` forgets the
    14	twist.  Conjugating this observation by `pic0ThetaType` gives an action on the
    15	Picard-zero functor over `L`; representability will transport it to the
    16	representing scheme.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	set_option autoImplicit false
    20	
    21	universe u
    22	
    23	open CategoryTheory
    24	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    25	
    26	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    27	
    28	variable {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
    29	
    30	/-- The structure morphism of the field-extension test functor. -/
    31	noncomputable abbrev pic0GaloisBaseMap :
    32	    Spec (CommRingCat.of L) ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k) :=
    33	  Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))
    34	
    35	/-- Restriction of an `L`-test to a `k`-test. -/
    36	noncomputable abbrev pic0GaloisRestrictTest :
    37	    Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) ⥤ Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) :=
    38	  Over.map (pic0GaloisBaseMap (k := k) (L := L))
    39	
    40	/-- Every `k`-algebra automorphism of `L` is invisible after composing with
    41	`Spec L ⟶ Spec k`. -/
    42	theorem pic0Galois_baseAut_comp (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
    43	    (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[k] L) L gamma).hom ≫
    44	        pic0GaloisBaseMap (k := k) (L := L) =
    45	      pic0GaloisBaseMap (k := k) (L := L) := by
    46	  rw [toSpecAut_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
    47	  congr 2
    48	  ext x
    49	  exact gamma⁻¹.commutes x
    50	
    51	/-- Twist `L`-tests by a `k`-algebra automorphism of `L`. -/
    52	noncomputable abbrev pic0TwistTestFunctor (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
    53	    Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) ⥤ Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)) :=
    54	  Over.map (toSpecAut (L ≃ₐ[k] L) L gamma).hom
    55	
    56	/-- Restriction to `k` identifies a twisted `L`-test with the original
    57	restricted test. -/
    58	noncomputable def pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
    59	    pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma ⋙
    60	        pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L) ≅
    61	      pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L) :=
    62	  (Over.mapComp _ _).symm ≪≫
    63	    Over.mapCongr _ _ (pic0Galois_baseAut_comp gamma)
    64	
    65	@[simp]
    66	theorem pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_hom_app_left
    67	    (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
    68	    ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom.app T).left = 𝟙 T.left := by
    69	  simp [pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso, Over.mapComp, Over.mapCongr]
    70	
    71	/-- A product twist is canonically the corresponding iterated twist. -/
    72	noncomputable def pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
    73	    pic0TwistTestFunctor (gamma * tau) ≅
    74	      pic0TwistTestFunctor tau ⋙ pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma :=
    75	  Over.mapCongr _ _ (toSpecAut_mul_hom (L ≃ₐ[k] L) L gamma tau) ≪≫
    76	    Over.mapComp _ _
    77	
    78	@[simp]
    79	theorem pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso_hom_app_left
    80	    (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
    81	    ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app T).left = 𝟙 T.left := by
    82	  simp [pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso, Over.mapComp, Over.mapCongr]
    83	
    84	/-- The identity twist is the identity functor. -/
    85	noncomputable def pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso :
    86	    pic0TwistTestFunctor (1 : L ≃ₐ[k] L) ≅ 𝟭 _ :=
    87	  Over.mapCongr _ _ (by rw [map_one]; rfl) ≪≫ Over.mapId _
    88	
    89	@[simp]
    90	theorem pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso_hom_app_left
    91	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
    92	    ((pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso (k := k) (L := L)).hom.app T).left =
    93	      𝟙 T.left := by
    94	  simp [pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso, Over.mapCongr, Over.mapId]
    95	
    96	theorem pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_one_hom_app
    97	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
    98	    (pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso (1 : L ≃ₐ[k] L)).hom.app T =
    99	      (pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).map
   100	        ((pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso (k := k) (L := L)).hom.app T) := by
   101	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   102	  simp only [pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_hom_app_left, Over.map_map_left,
   103	    pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso_hom_app_left]
   104	
   105	theorem pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_mul_hom_app
   106	    (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
   107	    (pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso (gamma * tau)).hom.app T =
   108	      (pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).map
   109	          ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app T) ≫
   110	        (pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom.app
   111	          ((pic0TwistTestFunctor tau).obj T) ≫
   112	        (pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso tau).hom.app T := by
   113	  apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   114	  simp only [Over.map_obj_left, pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_hom_app_left,
   115	    Over.comp_left, Over.map_map_left,
   116	    pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso_hom_app_left, Category.comp_id]
   117	  rfl
   118	
   119	section FunctorAction
   120	
   121	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
   122	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   123	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
   124	
   125	/-- The action on the `k`-Picard-zero functor restricted to `L`-tests. -/
   126	noncomputable def pic0GaloisActionRestricted (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   127	    (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).op ⋙
   128	        ((pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).op ⋙
   129	          pic0TypeFunctor C) ≅
   130	      (pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).op ⋙
   131	        pic0TypeFunctor C :=
   132	  (Functor.associator _ _ _).symm ≪≫
   133	    Functor.isoWhiskerRight
   134	      (NatIso.op (pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma)).symm
   135	      (pic0TypeFunctor C)
   136	
   137	theorem pic0GaloisActionRestricted_inv_app
   138	    (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))) :
   139	    (pic0GaloisActionRestricted C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op T) =
   140	      (pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   141	        ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom.app T).op := by
   142	  change _ ≫ 𝟙 _ = _
   143	  rw [Category.comp_id]
   144	  rfl
   145	
   146	theorem pic0GaloisActionRestricted_one_inv_app
   147	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)))
   148	    (x : ((pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).op ⋙
   149	      pic0TypeFunctor C).obj
   150	      (Opposite.op T)) :
   151	    (pic0GaloisActionRestricted C (1 : L ≃ₐ[k] L)).inv.app
   152	        (Opposite.op T) x =
   153	      (((pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).op ⋙
   154	        pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   155	        ((pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso (k := k) (L := L)).hom.app T).op) x := by
   156	  rw [pic0GaloisActionRestricted_inv_app,
   157	    pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_one_hom_app]
   158	  rfl
   159	
   160	private theorem pic0_map_op_comp_comp_apply
   161	    {W X Y Z : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k))}
   162	    (f : W ⟶ X) (g : X ⟶ Y) (h : Y ⟶ Z)
   163	    (x : (pic0TypeFunctor C).obj (Opposite.op Z)) :
   164	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).map (f ≫ g ≫ h).op x =
   165	      (pic0TypeFunctor C).map f.op
   166	        ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map g.op ((pic0TypeFunctor C).map h.op x)) := by
   167	  rw [op_comp, op_comp, Functor.map_comp, Functor.map_comp]
   168	  rfl
   169	
   170	theorem pic0GaloisActionRestricted_mul_inv_app

   173	      pic0TypeFunctor C).obj
   174	      (Opposite.op T)) :
   175	    (pic0GaloisActionRestricted C (gamma * tau)).inv.app
   176	        (Opposite.op T) x =
   177	      (((pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).op ⋙
   178	        pic0TypeFunctor C).map
   179	        ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app T).op)
   180	        ((pic0GaloisActionRestricted C gamma).inv.app
   181	          (Opposite.op ((pic0TwistTestFunctor tau).obj T))
   182	          ((pic0GaloisActionRestricted C tau).inv.app (Opposite.op T) x)) := by
   183	  rw [pic0GaloisActionRestricted_inv_app,
   184	    pic0GaloisActionRestricted_inv_app,
   185	    pic0GaloisActionRestricted_inv_app]

   187	    (pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso_mul_hom_app gamma tau T)
   188	  rw [h]

   190	    (((pic0GaloisRestrictTest (k := k) (L := L)).map
   191	      ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app T)).op) _
   192	  exact pic0_map_op_comp_comp_apply C

   194	      ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app T))
   195	    ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso gamma).hom.app
   196	      ((pic0TwistTestFunctor tau).obj T))
   197	    ((pic0GaloisRestrictTwistIso tau).hom.app T) x

   200	restricted action with `pic0ThetaType`. -/

   202	    (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).op ⋙
   203	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) ≅
   204	      pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
   205	  Functor.isoWhiskerLeft _ (pic0ThetaType k L C) ≪≫

   210	    (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)))

   212	    (pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op T) x =
   213	      (pic0ThetaType k L C).inv.app
   214	        (Opposite.op ((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj T))
   215	        ((pic0GaloisActionRestricted C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op T)
   216	          ((pic0ThetaType k L C).hom.app (Opposite.op T) x)) := by

   220	    (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L)))

   224	        ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app T).op

   253	variable (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))

   256	variable {J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))}

   258	
   259	/-- The morphism from the twisted representing object to the original one,
   260	obtained by applying the inverse functor action to the universal class. -/
   261	noncomputable def pic0GaloisTwistMor (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   262	    (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).obj J ⟶ J :=
   263	  rep.homEquiv.symm
   264	    ((pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op J)
   265	      (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J)))

   267	@[simp]
   268	theorem pic0Galois_homEquiv_twistMor (gamma : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   269	    rep.homEquiv (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma) =
   270	      (pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op J)
   271	        (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J)) :=
   272	  Equiv.apply_symm_apply _ _

   274	/-- The twist morphisms obey the field-automorphism group law in the slice. -/
   275	theorem pic0GaloisTwistMor_mul (gamma tau : L ≃ₐ[k] L) :
   276	    pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (gamma * tau) =
   277	      (pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app J ≫
   278	        (pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).map
   279	          (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau) ≫
   280	        pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep gamma := by
   281	  apply rep.homEquiv.injective
   282	  rw [pic0Galois_homEquiv_twistMor, rep.homEquiv_comp,
   283	    rep.homEquiv_comp, pic0Galois_homEquiv_twistMor]
   284	  change _ = (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).map
   285	    ((pic0TwistTestFunctorMulIso gamma tau).hom.app J).op
   286	      (((pic0TwistTestFunctor gamma).op ⋙
   287	        pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange k L).obj C)).map
   288	          (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau).op
   289	          ((pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv.app (Opposite.op J)
   290	            (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J))))
   291	  rw [← NatTrans.naturality_apply (pic0GaloisAction C gamma).inv
   292	    (pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep tau).op (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J))]
   293	  rw [← rep.homEquiv_eq, pic0Galois_homEquiv_twistMor]
   294	  exact pic0GaloisAction_mul_inv_app C gamma tau J
   295	    (rep.homEquiv (𝟙 J))

   298	theorem pic0GaloisTwistMor_one :
   299	    pic0GaloisTwistMor C rep (1 : L ≃ₐ[k] L) =
   300	      (pic0TwistTestFunctorOneIso (k := k) (L := L)).hom.app J := by

     9	/-!
    10	# The quotient-side bridge for finite Galois descent of Picard zero
    11	
    12	A specified finite Galois quotient represents equivariant maps after base
    13	change.  This file records that statement in the over-category.  It is the
    14	scheme-theoretic half of descending a representative of `pic0TypeFunctor`.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits
    22	open AlgebraicGeometry
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    25	
    26	/-- An equivariant map from the finite-Galois base change of an object over
    27	`Spec K` to a semilinearly acted `L`-scheme. -/
    28	structure GaloisEquivariantOver
    29	    {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    30	    {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    31	    (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    32	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) where
    33	  hom : pullback T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L))) ⟶ X
    34	  commutes : hom ≫ f =
    35	    pullback.snd T.hom (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K L)))
    36	  equivariant : (pullbackSemilinearGalAction K L T.hom).IsEquivariant rho hom
    37	
    38	namespace GaloisEquivariantOver
    39	
    40	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    41	  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    42	  (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
    43	
    44	/-- Pull an equivariant map back along a morphism over `Spec K`. -/
    45	noncomputable def precomp
    46	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
    47	    (h : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T) : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T' where
    48	  hom := pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w ≫ h.hom
    49	  commutes := by
    50	    rw [Category.assoc, h.commutes, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
    51	  equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    52	    T.hom T'.hom rho h.equivariant a.left a.w
    53	
    54	@[ext]
    55	theorem ext {T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))}
    56	    {h h' : GaloisEquivariantOver rho T} (hh : h.hom = h'.hom) : h = h' := by
    57	  cases h
    58	  cases h'
    59	  cases hh
    60	  rfl
    61	
    62	end GaloisEquivariantOver

    64	namespace GaloisQuotientWitness
    65	
    66	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    67	  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
    68	  {rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f}
    69	  {Y : Scheme.{u}} {g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)}
    70	
    71	/-- A finite-Galois quotient witness represents equivariant maps after base
    72	change, with no affineness assumption on the test object. -/
    73	noncomputable def overHomEquiv (w : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g)
    74	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
    75	    (T ⟶ Over.mk g) ≃ GaloisEquivariantOver rho T where
    76	  toFun a :=
    77	    { hom := pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom a.left a.w ≫ w.e.hom
    78	      commutes := by
    79	        rw [Category.assoc, w.over, pullbackBaseChange_snd]
    80	      equivariant := SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    81	        g T.hom rho w.equivariant a.left a.w }
    82	  invFun h :=
    83	    Over.homMk
    84	      (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose.1
    85	      (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose.2
    86	  left_inv a := by
    87	    apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
    88	    let h := pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom a.left a.w ≫ w.e.hom
    89	    let hw := w.universal T.left T.hom h
    90	      (by
    91	        dsimp [h]
    92	        rw [Category.assoc, w.over, pullbackBaseChange_snd])
    93	      (by
    94	        dsimp [h]
    95	        exact SemilinearGalAction.isEquivariant_pullbackBaseChange_comp
    96	          g T.hom rho w.equivariant a.left a.w)
    97	    have ha : pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom a.left a.w ≫ w.e.hom = h := rfl
    98	    have heq : hw.choose = ⟨a.left, a.w⟩ :=
    99	      hw.unique hw.choose_spec.1 ha
   100	    exact congrArg Subtype.val heq
   101	  right_inv h := by
   102	    apply GaloisEquivariantOver.ext rho
   103	    exact (w.universal T.left T.hom h.hom h.commutes h.equivariant).choose_spec.1
   104	
   105	/-- The quotient universal-property equivalence commutes with precomposition
   106	in the category of schemes over `Spec K`. -/
   107	theorem overHomEquiv_precomp (w : GaloisQuotientWitness rho Y g)
   108	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
   109	    (b : T ⟶ Over.mk g) :
   110	    w.overHomEquiv T' (a ≫ b) =
   111	      GaloisEquivariantOver.precomp rho a (w.overHomEquiv T b) := by
   112	  apply GaloisEquivariantOver.ext rho
   113	  change pullbackBaseChange K L g T'.hom (a.left ≫ b.left) _ ≫ w.e.hom =
   114	    pullbackBaseChange K L T.hom T'.hom a.left a.w ≫
   115	      (pullbackBaseChange K L g T.hom b.left b.w ≫ w.e.hom)
   116	  rw [pullbackBaseChange_comp K L g T.hom T'.hom b.left b.w a.left a.w,
   117	    Category.assoc]
   118	
   119	end GaloisQuotientWitness

   121	namespace StableAffineOpen
   122	
   123	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
   124	  {X : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
   125	  (rho : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
   126	
   127	/-- Under the orbit-in-an-affine-open hypothesis, the glued invariant-ring
   128	quotient represents equivariant maps after finite Galois base change. -/
   129	noncomputable def gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv
   130	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen]
   131	    (T : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))) :
   132	    (T ⟶ gluedQuotientOver rho) ≃ GaloisEquivariantOver rho T :=
   133	  (gluedGaloisQuotientWitness rho).toGaloisQuotientWitness.overHomEquiv T
   134	
   135	/-- The glued-quotient equivalence is natural under precomposition. -/
   136	theorem gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv_precomp
   137	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] [rho.OrbitsInAffineOpen]
   138	    {T T' : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))} (a : T' ⟶ T)
   139	    (b : T ⟶ gluedQuotientOver rho) :
   140	    gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv rho T' (a ≫ b) =
   141	      GaloisEquivariantOver.precomp rho a (gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv rho T b) :=
   142	  GaloisQuotientWitness.overHomEquiv_precomp
   143	    (gluedGaloisQuotientWitness rho).toGaloisQuotientWitness a b
   144	
   145	end StableAffineOpen

     9	# Conditional finite-Galois representability for Picard zero
    10	
    11	This is a conditional producer: it descends a finite-level representative only
    12	under the explicitly supplied orbit-in-an-affine-open instance.  It is not the
    13	arbitrary-field representability endpoint.
    14	-/
    15	
    16	set_option autoImplicit false
    17	
    18	universe u
    19	
    20	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    21	open AlgebraicGeometry
    22	open AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent
    23	
    24	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	variable {K L : Type u} [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra K L]
    29	
    30	/-- Conditional finite-Galois descent of a finite-level Picard-zero representative.
    31	
    32	The orbit-in-an-affine-open instance is the sole extra descent hypothesis here;
    33	this theorem does not claim arbitrary-field representability.
    34	-/
    35	noncomputable def pic0RepresentableBy_finiteGaloisDescent
    36	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K)))
    37	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    38	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    39	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]
    40	    {J : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of L))}
    41	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor ((baseChange K L).obj C)).RepresentableBy J)
    42	    [((pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep).OrbitsInAffineOpen)] :
    43	    (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy
    44	      (AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOver
    45	        (pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep)) where
    46	  homEquiv {T} :=
    47	    ((StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv
    48	      (pic0SemilinearGalActionOfRepresentableBy C rep) T).trans
    49	      (pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver C rep T).symm).trans
    50	      (pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv (L := L) C T).symm
    51	  homEquiv_comp {T T'} f v := by
    52	    apply (pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv (L := L) C T).injective
    53	    apply (pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver C rep T).injective
    54	    simp only [Equiv.trans_apply, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    55	    rw [StableAffineOpen.gluedQuotientOverHomEquiv_precomp]
    56	    rw [pic0GaloisInvariantEquiv_precomp]
    57	    rw [pic0GaloisInvariantEquivGaloisEquivariantOver_precomp]
    58	    simp only [Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
    59	
    60	end

    10	/-!
    11	# Finite subsets of quasi-projective schemes lie in affine opens
    12	
    13	This module derives `Scheme.FiniteInAffine` from projectivity over an affine
    14	base. It does not construct a quasi-projectivity witness for any Picard scheme.
    15	-/
    16	
    17	set_option autoImplicit false
    18	
    19	universe u
    20	
    21	open CategoryTheory Limits AlgebraicGeometry
    22	
    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme
    24	
    25	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along open immersions. -/
    26	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isOpenImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    27	    [IsOpenImmersion f] (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    28	  classical
    29	  intro s hs
    30	  obtain ⟨U, hU⟩ := hY (f.base '' s) (hs.image f.base)
    31	  letI : Fintype s := hs.fintype
    32	  obtain ⟨r, hr, hrle⟩ :=
    33	    AlgebraicJacobian.GaloisDescent.exists_basicOpen_le_of_finite U.2
    34	      (fun x : s => f.base x)
    35	      (fun x => hU ⟨x, x.2, rfl⟩)
    36	      (fun x => Scheme.Hom.mem_opensRange.mpr ⟨(x : X), rfl⟩)
    37	  refine ⟨⟨f ⁻¹ᵁ Y.basicOpen r,
    38	    (U.2.basicOpen r).preimage_of_isOpenImmersion f hrle⟩, ?_⟩
    39	  intro x hx
    40	  change f.base x ∈ Y.basicOpen r
    41	  exact hr ⟨x, hx⟩
    42	
    43	/-- `FiniteInAffine` descends along arbitrary immersions. -/
    44	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isImmersion {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    45	    [IsImmersion f] (hY : FiniteInAffine Y) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    46	  obtain ⟨Z, g₁, g₂, hg₁, hg₂, -⟩ :=
    47	    (AlgebraicGeometry.IsImmersion.isImmersion_iff_exists (f := f)).mp
    48	      (inferInstance : IsImmersion f)
    49	  haveI := hg₁
    50	  haveI := hg₂
    51	  exact finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom g₁
    52	    (finiteInAffine_of_isOpenImmersion g₂ hY)
    53	
    54	/-- Relative projective space over an affine base satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    55	theorem finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace (n : Type u) (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] :
    56	    FiniteInAffine (ProjectiveSpace n S) := by
    57	  haveI : IsAffineHom (ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt n S) := by
    58	    rw [ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt_eq_snd]
    59	    exact MorphismProperty.pullback_snd _ _ inferInstance
    60	  exact finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom (ProjectiveSpace.toProjInt n S)
    61	    (finiteInAffine_proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule n (ULift.{u} ℤ)))
    62	
    63	/-- A scheme projective over an affine base satisfies `FiniteInAffine`. -/
    64	theorem finiteInAffine_of_isProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine S] {π : X ⟶ S}
    65	    (h : π.IsProjective) : FiniteInAffine X := by
    66	  obtain ⟨n, -, i, hi, -⟩ := h
    67	  haveI := hi
    68	  exact finiteInAffine_of_isAffineHom i (finiteInAffine_projectiveSpace n S)
    69	
    70	end AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme

    10	/-!
    11	# Finite subsets of irreducible algebraic groups lie in affine opens
    12	
    13	This file formalizes the irreducible, algebraically closed core of
    14	[Stacks, Lemma 39.8.6](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B7S). Translation
    15	turns one affine neighborhood of the identity into finitely many dense open
    16	subsets. Irreducibility gives a common closed point, and translating back gives
    17	one affine open containing the prescribed rational points.
    18	
    19	The final theorem applies this argument to arbitrary finite sets of topological

    10	/-!
    11	# Projectivity of smooth proper curves
    12	
    13	A finite morphism to the projective line gives a closed immersion into a
    14	relative projective space. The existing finite-map construction therefore
    15	makes every smooth proper geometrically integral curve projective over its
    16	base field.

    31	/-- A smooth proper geometrically integral relative curve is projective over
    32	the base field. -/

    34	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    35	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    36	    [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by
    37	  obtain ⟨pi, hpi, hcomp⟩ := exists_isFinite_toP1 (C := C)
    38	  letI : IsFinite pi := hpi
    39	  exact isProjective_of_isFinite_toP1 C pi hcomp

    41	/-- Projectivity under the smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve
    42	hypotheses used by the algebraic Jacobian challenge. -/

    44	    (C : Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of k)))
    45	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    46	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : C.hom.IsProjective := by

     9	/-!
    10	# Projective morphisms
    11	
    12	This file supplies the universe-polymorphic geometric core of projectivity that

    14	a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional relative projective space.

    23	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    25	/-- A morphism is projective if it admits a closed immersion into a
    26	finite-dimensional relative projective space over its target. -/
    27	def Scheme.Hom.IsProjective {X S : Scheme.{u}} (pi : X ⟶ S) : Prop :=
    28	  ∃ (n : Type u) (_ : Finite n) (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)),
    29	    IsClosedImmersion i ∧ i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi
    30	
    31	namespace Scheme.Hom.IsProjective

    33	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} {pi : X ⟶ S}
    34	
    35	/-- Projective morphisms are proper. -/
    36	theorem isProper (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsProper pi := by
    37	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    38	  letI : Finite n := hn
    39	  haveI := hi
    40	  rw [← hcomp]
    41	  infer_instance
    42	
    43	/-- Projective morphisms are locally of finite type. -/
    44	theorem locallyOfFiniteType (h : pi.IsProjective) : LocallyOfFiniteType pi :=
    45	  haveI := h.isProper
    46	  inferInstance
    47	
    48	/-- Projective morphisms are separated. -/
    49	theorem isSeparated (h : pi.IsProjective) : IsSeparated pi :=
    50	  haveI := h.isProper
    51	  inferInstance
    52	
    53	/-- Projective morphisms are universally closed. -/
    54	theorem universallyClosed (h : pi.IsProjective) : UniversallyClosed pi :=
    55	  haveI := h.isProper
    56	  inferInstance

    58	/-- A closed immersion into a projective scheme is projective. -/
    59	theorem comp_isClosedImmersion (h : pi.IsProjective) {Y : Scheme.{u}}
    60	    (j : Y ⟶ X) [IsClosedImmersion j] : (j ≫ pi).IsProjective := by
    61	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    62	  letI : Finite n := hn
    63	  haveI := hi
    64	  exact ⟨n, hn, j ≫ i, inferInstance, by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp]⟩

    66	/-- The comparison morphism from the base-changed source to the corresponding
    67	base change of its ambient projective space. -/
    68	private def baseChangeLift {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) {n : Type u}
    69	    (i : X ⟶ ℙ(n; S)) (hcomp : i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S) = pi) :
    70	    pullback pi g ⟶ ℙ(n; S') :=
    71	  (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).lift
    72	    (pullback.fst pi g ≫ i) (pullback.snd pi g)
    73	    (by rw [Category.assoc, hcomp, pullback.condition])

    75	/-- Projective morphisms are stable under arbitrary base change. -/
    76	theorem baseChange (h : pi.IsProjective) {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : S' ⟶ S) :
    77	    (pullback.snd pi g).IsProjective := by
    78	  obtain ⟨n, hn, i, hi, hcomp⟩ := h
    79	  letI : Finite n := hn
    80	  haveI := hi
    81	  refine ⟨n, hn, baseChangeLift g i hcomp, ?_, ?_⟩
    82	  · have h1 : baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S') =
    83	        pullback.snd pi g := IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _
    84	    have hsq : IsPullback (baseChangeLift g i hcomp) (pullback.fst pi g)
    85	        (ProjectiveSpace.map n g) i := by
    86	      have hbig : IsPullback
    87	          (baseChangeLift g i hcomp ≫ (ℙ(n; S') ↘ S'))
    88	          (pullback.fst pi g) g (i ≫ (ℙ(n; S) ↘ S)) := by
    89	        rw [h1, hcomp]
    90	        exact (IsPullback.of_hasPullback pi g).flip
    91	      exact IsPullback.of_right hbig
    92	        (IsPullback.lift_fst _ _ _ _)
    93	        (ProjectiveSpace.isPullback_map n g).flip
    94	    exact MorphismProperty.of_isPullback hsq.flip hi
    95	  · exact IsPullback.lift_snd _ _ _ _

    12	# Finite-separable points of a smooth curve
    13	
    14	A point over an algebraic extension of a finitely presented `k`-scheme spreads to one finite
    15	subextension.  Applying this to a point of a challenge curve over a separable closure produces a
    16	point over a finite separable extension, without a rational-point or divisor-degree hypothesis.
    17	
    18	The distinction is important over imperfect fields: an arbitrary closed point of a smooth curve
    19	can have inseparable residue field, but a separable closed point can still be chosen.
    20	
    21	## Main declarations
    22	
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finiteSubextension_point_of_point` spreads a point over an algebraic
    24	  extension to a finite subextension.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_separableClosure_finSubext_point` keeps the resulting finite stage
    26	  inside a fixed separable closure.
    27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_separable_point` produces a finite separable extension over
    28	  which any challenge curve has a rational point.
    29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_finite_galois_point` enlarges that stage to its finite Galois normal
    30	  closure while preserving the point.
    31	-/

    68	/-- A point over an algebraic extension of a finitely presented `k`-scheme is already defined
    69	over one finite subextension.
    70	
    71	The finite subextensions form the cofiltered affine diagram `deltaSchemeDiagram`, whose limit is
    72	`Spec Omega`.  Local finite presentation of `X/k` makes the point factor through one stage via
    73	`Scheme.exists_pi_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation`.  If `Omega/k` is separable, the
    74	returned stage is a finite separable extension by `DatG0.isSeparable_finSubext`. -/
    75	theorem exists_finiteSubextension_point_of_point {k Omega : Type u} [Field k] [Field Omega]
    76	    [Algebra k Omega] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic k Omega] [Algebra.IsSeparable k Omega]
    77	    {X : Over (Spec (.of k))} [LocallyOfFinitePresentation X.hom]
    78	    (a : Spec (.of Omega) ⟶ X.left)
    79	    (ha : a ≫ X.hom = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Omega))) :
    80	    ∃ L : FinSubext k Omega, Nonempty (overSpec k L.1 ⟶ X) := by
    81	  let E := deltaSchemeDiagram (k := k) (K := Omega)
    82	  let D := E ⋙ Over.forget (Spec (.of k))
    83	  let t : D ⟶ (Functor.const _).obj (Spec (.of k)) :=
    84	    { app := fun i => (E.obj i).hom
    85	      naturality := fun {i j} h => by
    86	        change (E.map h).left ≫ (E.obj j).hom = (E.obj i).hom ≫ 𝟙 _
    87	        rw [Category.comp_id]
    88	        exact Over.w (E.map h) }
    89	  let c : Cone D := Scheme.Spec.mapCone (deltaCocone (k := k) (K := Omega)).op
    90	  have hc : IsLimit c :=
    91	    isLimitOfPreserves Scheme.Spec (deltaIsColimit (k := k) (K := Omega)).op
    92	  letI (i : (FinSubext k Omega)ᵒᵖ) : IsAffine (D.obj i) := by
    93	    change IsAffine (Spec (.of (unop i).1))
    94	    infer_instance
    95	  letI (i : (FinSubext k Omega)ᵒᵖ) : CompactSpace (D.obj i) := by
    96	    change CompactSpace (Spec (.of (unop i).1))
    97	    infer_instance
    98	  letI (i : (FinSubext k Omega)ᵒᵖ) : QuasiSeparatedSpace (D.obj i) := by
    99	    change QuasiSeparatedSpace (Spec (.of (unop i).1))
   100	    infer_instance
   101	  letI {i j : (FinSubext k Omega)ᵒᵖ} (h : i ⟶ j) : IsAffineHom (D.map h) := by
   102	    apply isAffineHom_of_isAffine
   103	  have hct : c.π ≫ t = (Functor.const _).map (a ≫ X.hom) := by
   104	    ext i
   105	    change Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (IntermediateField.val (unop i).1).toRingHom) ≫
   106	      (overSpec k (unop i).1).hom = a ≫ X.hom
   107	    rw [ha, overSpec_hom, ← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp]
   108	    congr 2
   109	  obtain ⟨i, g, _, hg⟩ :=
   110	    Scheme.exists_π_app_comp_eq_of_locallyOfFinitePresentation D t X.hom c hc a hct
   111	  exact ⟨unop i, ⟨Over.homMk g hg⟩⟩
   112	
   113	/-- Every challenge curve has a point over a finite subextension of its separable closure.
   114	
   115	First take a point of the base-changed curve over a separable closure, using smooth relative
   116	dimension one and geometric irreducibility for nonemptiness.  Its projection to `C` spreads to a
   117	finite stage by `exists_finiteSubextension_point_of_point`; every such stage inside the separable
   118	closure is separable.  Keeping the stage bundled is what permits the normal-closure enlargement
   119	in `exists_finite_galois_point`. -/
   120	theorem exists_separableClosure_finSubext_point {k : Type u} [Field k]
   121	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   122	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   123	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   124	    ∃ L : FinSubext k (SeparableClosure k), Nonempty (overSpec k L.1 ⟶ C) := by
   125	  let Omega := SeparableClosure k
   126	  letI : Algebra.IsAlgebraic k Omega :=
   127	    separableClosure.isAlgebraic k (AlgebraicClosure k)
   128	  letI : Algebra.IsSeparable k Omega :=
   129	    separableClosure.isSeparable k (AlgebraicClosure k)
   130	  letI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeBundle C Omega).hom :=
   131	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChangeBundle C Omega
   132	  letI : GeometricallyIrreducible (baseChangeBundle C Omega).hom :=
   133	    instGeometricallyIrreducibleBaseChangeBundle C Omega
   134	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ :=
   135	    SeparablyClosed.exists_rationalPoint_of_smoothOfRelativeDimension_one
   136	      (baseChangeBundle C Omega).hom
   137	  let fst' : (baseChangeBundle C Omega).left ⟶ C.left :=
   138	    pullback.fst C.hom (overSpec k Omega).hom
   139	  let a : Spec (.of Omega) ⟶ C.left := q ≫ fst'
   140	  have hcond : fst' ≫ C.hom =
   141	      (baseChangeBundle C Omega).hom ≫ (overSpec k Omega).hom :=
   142	    pullback.condition
   143	  have haOver : a ≫ C.hom = (overSpec k Omega).hom := by
   144	    dsimp only [a]
   145	    rw [Category.assoc, hcond, ← Category.assoc]
   146	    rw [hq, Category.id_comp]
   147	  have ha : a ≫ C.hom =
   148	      Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k Omega)) :=
   149	    haOver.trans (overSpec_hom k Omega)
   150	  obtain ⟨L, hp⟩ := exists_finiteSubextension_point_of_point a ha
   151	  exact ⟨L, hp⟩
   152	
   153	/-- Every challenge curve acquires a rational point over a finite separable extension. -/
   154	theorem exists_finite_separable_point {k : Type u} [Field k]
   155	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   156	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   157	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   158	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
   159	      (_ : Module.Finite k L) (_ : Algebra.IsSeparable k L),
   160	      Nonempty (overSpec k L ⟶ C) := by
   161	  obtain ⟨L, hp⟩ := exists_separableClosure_finSubext_point C
   162	  letI : Module.Finite k L.1 := L.2
   163	  letI : Algebra.IsSeparable k L.1 := isSeparable_finSubext L
   164	  exact ⟨L.1, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, hp⟩
   165	
   166	/-- Every challenge curve acquires a rational point over a finite Galois extension.
   167	
   168	Take the finite stage inside `SeparableClosure k` produced above and replace it by its normal
   169	closure in the same ambient field.  Mathlib supplies finite dimensionality and the Galois
   170	instance for this normal closure.  The original point pushes forward along the inclusion of
   171	finite stages via `DatG0.deltaSchemeMap`.
   172	
   173	No rational-point, divisor-degree, separability, or Galois hypothesis is added to the curve. -/
   174	theorem exists_finite_galois_point {k : Type u} [Field k]
   175	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   176	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
   177	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
   178	    ∃ (L : Type u) (_ : Field L) (_ : Algebra k L)
   179	      (_ : Module.Finite k L) (_ : IsGalois k L),
   180	      Nonempty (overSpec k L ⟶ C) := by
   181	  obtain ⟨L, ⟨p⟩⟩ := exists_separableClosure_finSubext_point C
   182	  let K : FinSubext k (SeparableClosure k) :=
   183	    ⟨IntermediateField.normalClosure k L.1 (SeparableClosure k), inferInstance⟩
   184	  have hle : L.1 ≤ K.1 := IntermediateField.le_normalClosure L.1
   185	  letI : Module.Finite k K.1 := K.2
   186	  letI : IsGalois k K.1 := by
   187	    dsimp only [K]
   188	    infer_instance
   189	  exact ⟨K.1, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance, inferInstance,
   190	    ⟨deltaSchemeMap hle ≫ p⟩⟩
   191	
   192	end

     9	/-!
    10	# Category-correct ambient contract for the rank-one Picard route
    11	
    12	The rank-one locus lives in degree `genus C`, not in `pic0`. This module installs the concrete
    13	ambient maps that the later open-locus restriction must consume:
    14	
    15	* `abelDivAffTrans` maps the widened degree-`n` divisor functor to `picDegLayerFunctor C n`;
    16	* `abelDivAffSigma` extends a represented slice map to the ambient big-site presheaf;
    17	* `abelDivAffGenusSigma` specializes the map using the canonical genus representation.
    18	
    19	The future public `PicRankOneOpen` must therefore be a subfunctor of
    20	`picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C)`, and `DivRankOneOpen` must be an open of
    21	`divRepAffGenusScheme C`. Its `rankOneAbel` is the restriction of
    22	`abelDivAffGenusSigma`, after applying the corresponding Sigma extension. No placeholder locus,
    23	inverse, representability witness, or endgame theorem is postulated here.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    28	
    29	universe u
    30	
    31	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
    32	
    33	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    34	
    35	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {n : ℕ}
    36	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    37	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    38	
    39	noncomputable section
    40	
    41	variable (C n) in
    42	/-- The widened Abel transformation into the intrinsic degree-`n` Picard layer. -/
    43	def abelDivAffTrans : divFunctorAff C n ⟶ picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ) where
    44	  app T := ↾fun s => ⟨abelDivAff' C n T.unop s, fun K _ _ t => degAt_abelDivAff' s t⟩
    45	  naturality T T' g := by
    46	    ext s
    47	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
    48	    exact (picEtMap_abelDivAff' g.unop s).symm
    49	
    50	@[simp]
    51	lemma abelDivAffTrans_app_coe
    52	    (T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ) (s : divFamZarAff C n T.unop) :
    53	    ((abelDivAffTrans C n).app T s).1 = abelDivAff' C n T.unop s :=
    54	  rfl
    55	
    56	variable (C n) in
    57	/-- Extend a represented widened Abel map from the slice over `Spec k` to the big site. -/
    58	def abelDivAffSigma {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    59	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) :
    60	    yoneda.obj D.left ⟶
    61	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (n : ℤ)) :=
    62	  rep.toSigmaExtension ≫ Over.sigmaExtensionNat (abelDivAffTrans C n)
    63	
    64	@[simp]
    65	lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_fst {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    66	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    67	    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    68	    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).1 = x ≫ D.hom :=
    69	  rfl
    70	
    71	@[simp]
    72	lemma abelDivAffSigma_app_coe {D : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    73	    (rep : (divFunctorAff C n).RepresentableBy D) (T : Schemeᵒᵖ)
    74	    (x : T.unop ⟶ D.left) :
    75	    ((abelDivAffSigma C n rep).app T x).2.1 =
    76	      abelDivAff' C n (Over.mk (x ≫ D.hom)) (rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk x rfl)) :=
    77	  rfl

    79	variable (C) in
    80	/-- The ambient genus-degree Abel map on the canonical represented widened divisor scheme.
    81	
    82	This is the map that the future rank-one divisor open must restrict. It is not itself claimed to
    83	be an open immersion. -/
    84	def abelDivAffGenusSigma :
    85	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶
    86	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ)) :=
    87	  abelDivAffSigma C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C)
    88

    37	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}

    43	/-! ## Sigma-extension isomorphisms -/
    44	
    45	/-- Sigma extension preserves natural isomorphisms of slice presheaves. -/
    46	noncomputable def sigmaExtensionIso {F G : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u}
    47	    (e : F ≅ G) :
    48	    Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) F ≅
    49	      Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) G where
    50	  hom := Over.sigmaExtensionNat e.hom
    51	  inv := Over.sigmaExtensionNat e.inv
    52	  hom_inv_id := by
    53	    ext T x
    54	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    55	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk a) (e.hom_inv_id_app_apply _ x)
    56	  inv_hom_id := by
    57	    ext T x
    58	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    59	    exact congrArg (Sigma.mk a) (e.inv_hom_id_app_apply _ x)
    60	
    61	/-- A representation on the slice extends to an isomorphism between the ambient Yoneda
    62	presheaf of its representing object and the sigma extension. -/
    63	noncomputable def representableBySigmaIso
    64	    {F : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    65	    (rep : F.RepresentableBy J) :
    66	    yoneda.obj J.left ≅ Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) F where
    67	  hom := rep.toSigmaExtension
    68	  inv :=
    69	    { app := fun T => TypeCat.ofHom fun x => (rep.homEquiv.symm x.2).left
    70	      naturality := by
    71	        intro T T' f
    72	        ext x
    73	        rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    74	        let q : Over.mk (f.unop ≫ a) ⟶ Over.mk a := Over.homMk f.unop rfl
    75	        exact (congrArg Over.Hom.left
    76	          (rep.comp_homEquiv_symm x q)).symm }
    77	  hom_inv_id := by
    78	    ext T v
    79	    exact congrArg Over.Hom.left (rep.homEquiv.symm_apply_apply
    80	      (Over.homMk v rfl : Over.mk (v ≫ J.hom) ⟶ J))
    81	  inv_hom_id := by
    82	    ext T x
    83	    rcases x with ⟨a, x⟩
    84	    let g := rep.homEquiv.symm x
    85	    have hga : g.left ≫ J.hom = a := g.w
    86	    refine Over.sigmaExtension_ext F hga ?_
    87	    change F.map (Over.mkCongr hga).op x =
    88	      rep.homEquiv (Over.homMk g.left rfl : Over.mk (g.left ≫ J.hom) ⟶ J)
    89	    rw [← rep.homEquiv.apply_symm_apply x]
    90	    rw [← rep.homEquiv_comp]
    91	    exact congrArg rep.homEquiv (Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl)

    95	/-- The Yoneda range of an open immersion is represented by its source.  Here the range is
    96	identified with the exact divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    97	noncomputable def rankOneDivisorOpenRepresentableBy
    98	    (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

   100	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi).toFunctor.RepresentableBy

   104	        have hy : y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h ∈
   105	            (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj (op T) :=
   106	          ⟨y, rfl⟩
   107	        rw [h.carrier_eq] at hy
   108	        exact hy⟩
   109	      invFun := fun x => Classical.choose
   110	        (rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization pi h x)
   111	      left_inv := fun y => by
   112	        apply Over.OverMorphism.ext
   113	        letI : IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) :=
   114	          divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion pi h
   115	        apply (cancel_mono (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)).mp
   116	        exact congrArg Over.Hom.left (Classical.choose_spec
   117	          (rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization pi h
   118	            ⟨y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h, by
   119	              have hy : y ≫ divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h ∈
   120	                  (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj (op T) :=
   121	                ⟨y, rfl⟩

   125	        apply Subtype.ext
   126	        exact Classical.choose_spec
   127	          (rankOneRepresenterRestriction_factorization pi h x) }

   129	    apply Subtype.ext
   130	    exact Category.assoc f y (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h)

   132	/-- The canonical Abel map and canonical evaluation divisor form an isomorphism already on the
   133	slice.  Its sigma extension is `canonicalRankOneAbelIso`. -/
   134	noncomputable def canonicalRankOneAbelSliceIso :
   135	    (divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter (divRepAffP1Map C)).toFunctor ≅
   136	      (PicRankOneOpen (divRepAffP1Map C)).toFunctor where
   137	  hom := rankOneAbelRepresented (divRepAffP1Map C)
   138	  inv := canonicalRankOneRepresenterTrans (C := C)
   139	  hom_inv_id := by

   141	    apply rankOneAbelRepresented_app_injective (divRepAffP1Map C) T.unop
   142	    exact canonicalRankOneRepresenterTrans_abel

   149	noncomputable def picRankOneOpenRepresentableBy

   156	/-! ## Translation by a base class of degree `genus C` -/
   157	
   158	/-- Base classes which translate degree zero into the genus-degree layer. -/
   159	abbrev PicRankOneTranslatorIndex :=
   160	  {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CechPic // classDeg k L = (genus C : ℤ)}
   161	
   162	/-- Multiplication by a translator, at one test object. -/
   163	noncomputable def pic0GenusTranslationEquiv
   164	    (a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C)) (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) :
   165	    pic0Subgroup C T ≃ picDegLayer C (genus C : ℤ) T where
   166	  toFun lam := ⟨lam.1 * thetaFamily C a.1 T, fun K _ _ t => by
   167	    rw [degAt_mul, lam.2 K t, degAt_thetaFamily, zero_add, a.2]⟩
   168	  invFun lam := ⟨lam.1 * (thetaFamily C a.1 T)⁻¹,
   169	    mem_pic0Subgroup_iff.mpr fun K _ _ t => by
   170	      rw [degAt_mul, degAt_inv, degAt_thetaFamily, lam.2 K t, a.2]
   171	      ring⟩
   172	  left_inv lam := Subtype.ext (mul_inv_cancel_right _ _)
   173	  right_inv lam := Subtype.ext (inv_mul_cancel_right _ _)

   175	/-- Multiplication by a translator is the natural isomorphism from `Pic^0` to the genus-degree
   176	Picard layer.  It is the degree-specialized, one-fold form of `mulThetaPowNatIso`. -/
   177	noncomputable def pic0GenusTranslationIso (a : PicRankOneTranslatorIndex (C := C)) :
   178	    pic0TypeFunctor C ≅ picDegLayerFunctor C (genus C : ℤ) :=
   179	  NatIso.ofComponents (fun T => (pic0GenusTranslationEquiv (C := C) a T.unop).toIso) (by
   180	    intro T T' f
   181	    ext lam
   182	    refine Subtype.ext ?_
   183	    have key :

Read-only audit complete. No files or index changed.

Shortest honest chain is already present:

```lean
J.hom.IsProjective
  -> Scheme.finiteInAffine_of_isProjective
  -> Scheme.orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine
  -> pic0RepresentableBy_finiteGaloisDescent
```

The last consumer is [Pic0FiniteGaloisRepresentable.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0FiniteGaloisRepresentable.lean:35); the two generic links are [QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/QuasiProjectiveFiniteInAffine.lean:64) and [FiniteInAffine.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/FiniteInAffine.lean:66). This gives the exact target action with no further equivariance work.

What is missing is genuinely geometric: bare `rep` supplies neither `J.hom.IsProjective` nor `FiniteInAffine J.left`. Even `JacobianData` adds only `GrpObj J`, `LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom`, and `QuasiCompact J.hom` ([JacobianData.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/JacobianData.lean:87)); none entails the needed property. The finite-Galois-point theorem only gives a point on `C_L`, not geometry of `J`.

The alternative group theorem, `finiteInAffine_of_isAlgClosed_of_irreducible`, requires `[IsAlgClosed L]`, `[LocallyOfFiniteType J.hom]`, `[IrreducibleSpace J.left]`, and `[GrpObj J]` ([GroupAffineOpen.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Descent/GroupAffineOpen.lean:162)). It cannot apply at a nontrivial finite Galois stage because `L` is not algebraically closed. Mathlib supplies no quasi-projectivity API that closes this gap.

Recommended bounded non-wrapper theorem:

```lean
theorem finiteInAffine_of_geometricallyIrreducible_group
    (G : Over (Spec (.of L))) [GrpObj G]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType G.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible G.hom] :
    Scheme.FiniteInAffine G.left
```

This is the arbitrary-field descent/generalization of the existing algebraically-closed group argument, not a Picard wrapper. It would be consumed immediately by `orbitsInAffineOpen_of_finiteInAffine` for the Pic0 action once the finite-stage spread records the natural group, lft, and geometric-irreducibility certificates. The remaining missing finite-stage data are exactly those noted in [Pic0CriticalPath.lean](/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/Pic0CriticalPath.lean:149).
